newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Schindler sees lower 1996 net profit.
newsitem.headline: Schindler sees lower 1996 net profit.

text.p: Swiss elevator and escalator maker Schindler Holding AG said it expected its 1996 profit to be slightly lower as compared to 1995.

"Due to a number of factors, particularly high nonrecurring costs, the consensus from today's prospective is that the consolidated net profit will be slightly lower than a year ago," Schindler said in a letter to shareholders.
It also said that the expected trend improvement in the group's core business lines will be reflected in the operating result.

"Given unchanged economic baseline conditions and foreign exchange relations, Schindler reaffirms its objective of returning to 1993/94 profit levels (around 160 million Swiss francs) by the end of 1997, excluding non-recurring costs," it said.

Schindler said operating results before restructuring charges in its core business of elevators and escalators would rise in 1996. It said its SPRINT programme to boost productivity in Europe would cost at least 35 million francs this year.
Some 1,000 jobs would be eliminated this year, of which 900 had already been cut by the end of July, it said.
It said rolling stock profit would decline noticeably this year because of lower production volume and prices.
But a 247 million franc order for tilting trains placed by the Swiss national railways in July would help boost capacity utilisation. Its impact on jobs would be greatest in 1998 to 2000, it said.
It said its ALSO computing subsidiary expected clearly lower operating profits in 1996 due to business development costs in Germany and project postponements among customers.
